personas.background: Grew up in Birmingham, moved to Leeds for university, stayed. Has been running for seven years, started with parkrun and worked up to trail running. Naturally sociable and enthusiastic — she tends to be the one who organises social events and checks in on people. Works long clinic hours but protects Sunday mornings fiercely.

food.value: post-run brunch over pub — prefers eggs and coffee to a pint

activities.value: prefers routes with a clear summit or destination over loops

social.value: enjoys the group coffee stop more than the run itself sometimes

domain_specific.value: prefers organised races over casual group runs — needs a goal to train toward

preference_history.trigger: Signed up for a half marathon after Cass's challenge — the target changed her training mindset entirely

speaking_quirks: starts excited messages with ALL CAPS or exclamation-heavy openers
uses 'honestly' or 'oh my god' as filler emphasis
strings multiple emoji together at end of messages

personas.occupation: Secondary school PE teacher and cross-country coach
personas.background: From Sheffield, always been sporty — rugby through school, switched to running in his late twenties after a knee injury ruled out contact sport. Competitive by instinct but tries to mask it in group settings. Has been with the Ridgeline Runners since near the beginning. Practical, no-fuss communicator.

food.value: post-run pub rather than cafe — a pint is non-negotiable after 15km+

activities.value: prefers technical trails with elevation over flat routes — bores easily on tarmac

social.value: would rather talk times and segments than personal life on runs

domain_specific.value: sceptical of running tech — relies on feel over gadgets

preference_history.old_value: goes out hard, fades in the second half
preference_history.new_value: negative splits — deliberately holds back early and builds
preference_history.trigger: Listened to an endurance coaching podcast while recovering from a cold — changed how he thinks about effort distribution

speaking_quirks: uses 'lads' as a default address for the whole group regardless of gender
drops subject pronouns at start of sentences ('Did 19km this morning. Felt decent.')
makes brief, un-elaborated observations that land as dry humour

personas.occupation: UX designer at a fintech startup
personas.background: Japanese-British, grew up in London, moved to Leeds three years ago for a job. Joined the group as a way to meet people outside work. Quiet and observant; says less but means more. Runs efficiently and quietly — rarely the fastest but almost never drops out. Dislikes crowds and prolonged social obligations but values this group specifically.

food.value: skips post-run social stops — prefers going straight home to eat and decompress

activities.value: prefers solo or small-group runs over the full group — less noise, more focus

social.value: values the group but finds the post-run social time draining rather than restorative

domain_specific.value: takes trail running very seriously — studies routes in advance and does not like improvising

preference_history.new_value: proper trail shoes with grip for wet and technical ground
preference_history.trigger: Slipped badly on a wet descent during session 3's run — bought trail shoes that week

speaking_quirks: responds with single complete sentences ending in full stops
never uses exclamation marks or emoji
uses precise technical vocabulary — 'descent,' 'elevation gain,' 'cadence' — even in casual messages

personas.background: Grew up in Bristol, has lived all over the place for work, settled in Leeds five years ago. Came to running late — started at 38 as stress relief between assignments. Opinionated and articulate, tends to hold court at post-run stops. Appreciates the discipline of running but is not particularly competitive about times — he runs to think.

food.value: pub stop after long runs — passionate about real ale and proper food

activities.value: prefers scenic routes with interesting terrain over pure speed routes

social.value: enjoys post-run conversation as much as the run — sometimes more

domain_specific.value: suspicious of wearable tech that gamifies running — prefers to run by feel and scenery

preference_history.old_value: pub pint immediately after any run over 12km
preference_history.new_value: electrolytes and food first, then pub if the group is staying
preference_history.trigger: Bad cramping episode mid-run in session 4 — Nadia identified poor recovery nutrition as the likely cause

speaking_quirks: opens messages with 'Right so' or 'Here's the thing'
uses vivid, slightly over-the-top descriptive language for terrain and conditions
drops in references to food and drink when discussing anything involving effort

personas.background: From Leeds originally, never left. Joined the running group two years ago after a colleague recommended it. The social glue of the group — always remembers birthdays, checks in after difficult runs, organises the WhatsApp polls. Competitive but self-deprecating about it. Has a habit of talking too much when nervous, especially on climbs.

food.value: cafe brunch over pub — specifically likes a good flat white and avocado toast

activities.value: prefers running with company over solo — finds motivation drops significantly alone

social.value: values the post-run coffee just as much as the run itself

domain_specific.value: enjoys signing up for group races more than individual ones — the shared experience matters more than the result

preference_history.old_value: one group run per month was enough
preference_history.new_value: two Sundays plus one midweek run per month
preference_history.trigger: Enjoyed the first midweek run so much it reset her expectations — the smaller group and midweek timing suited her

speaking_quirks: uses 'haha' mid-sentence even when only mildly amused
often ends messages with a question to keep the conversation going
uses 'we' even when describing personal achievements — 'we smashed that climb'

personas.occupation: GP, partner at a Leeds practice
personas.background: From Edinburgh, moved to Leeds for medical school, stayed. Took up running in his late thirties as a cardiovascular maintenance activity — very honest with himself that it is health-motivated rather than passion-driven. Precise and measured in everything he does, including running. Sometimes gives unsolicited medical context that the group finds either reassuring or patronising depending on the day.

food.value: tends to skip the post-run pub stop on medical grounds — avoids alcohol after long efforts

activities.value: prefers consistent aerobic effort over intervals — dislikes erratic pace variation

social.value: appreciates the group but rarely initiates social contact outside of runs

domain_specific.value: uses a heart rate monitor religiously — trains strictly by zones

preference_history.old_value: skips stretching — always too tired or rushed
preference_history.trigger: Developed a minor hamstring strain he'd been dismissing — finally took Nadia's advice seriously

speaking_quirks: uses formal medical or precise phrasing even in casual messages ('I would suggest', 'the data indicates')
never uses contractions when making a point ('I would not' rather than 'I wouldn't')
adds brief factual caveats or context to others' statements, unprompted

edges.history_summary: Nadia and Tom started the Ridgeline Runners together three years ago after meeting at a parkrun. They share the WhatsApp admin duties and generally agree on routes and logistics, though Tom is more competitive and Nadia more social.

Nadia recruited Yuki after seeing her at a parkrun and noticing her efficient form. They occasionally do mid-week runs together in smaller groups. Nadia appreciates Yuki's focus; Yuki appreciates Nadia's practical injury advice.
Rafe and Nadia get on well — they both enjoy the social side of running and often end up sitting together at post-run stops. Nadia helped Rafe when he had cramping issues on a long run.

Cass and Nadia have become close friends beyond running — they occasionally meet for coffee outside the group. Cass sees Nadia as the group's emotional centre; Nadia sees Cass as easy, uncomplicated company.
Nadia and Leo have a collegial warmth based on both working in healthcare. They occasionally discuss running injuries from a professional standpoint but are not socially close outside the group.
shared_events: injury assessment discussions on the trail

edges.history_summary: Tom and Yuki have never spent much time together one-on-one. They run at a similar pace on technical terrain but have little else in common conversationally. Tom finds her quietness a bit hard to read; she finds his bluntness occasionally abrasive.
Tom and Rafe enjoy trading opinions — Tom thinks Rafe overcomplicates everything, Rafe thinks Tom is too narrowly focused on times. The friction is mostly good-natured.
Tom and Cass are friendly but not particularly close — Cass occasionally teases Tom about his competitive nature; Tom tolerates it with a dry grin.
Tom and Leo share a no-nonsense communication style and mutual respect, but neither seeks the other out socially. They occasionally exchange brief technical notes about training.
Yuki and Rafe have little in common — she is quiet and data-focused, he is verbose and social. They are perfectly civil but would not choose to run together without the group.
Cass has made an effort with Yuki and they have a warm dynamic on runs — Cass chats; Yuki listens and occasionally responds with a dry observation that Cass finds funny.

Yuki and Leo have the least interaction in the group — both are introverted, both arrive and depart efficiently. They occasionally exchange data-related notes (elevation, heart rate zones) via the group chat.
Rafe and Cass enjoy each other's company a lot — they are both social, warm, and talkative. They tend to fall to the back of the group on long climbs and chat the whole way up.

Rafe and Leo have a recurring mild friction — Leo sometimes offers medical or nutritional notes that Rafe interprets as unsolicited lecturing. Rafe's more expansive, intuitive approach to running irritates Leo's precision-oriented style. They are cordial but occasionally pointed with each other.
shared_events: post-run discussions where they disagree on training philosophy

edges.history_summary: Cass finds Leo a bit serious but likes him — she occasionally tries to draw him into social conversation and he occasionally obliges with a dry observation. They get on better than their personalities suggest.

group_norms.norm_text: Everyone does their own stretches and cool-down after a run — the group doesn't wait around as a unit
Post-run coffee or pub stop is the expected thing after longer Sunday runs
Routes and start times go out in the group chat at least 48 hours before each run
Everyone is on Strava and segments are fair game for competitive comments
